owen: FYI hitting a weird combo of issues running the Redwood JS SDK inside an Expo devclient (RN 0.72 + Hermes). Two symptoms: `global.crypto.getRandomValues` missing, and streaming responses via fetch pipe into a reader fail with "reader.read is not a function". minimal stack: `TypeError: global.crypto.getRandomValues is not a function` then later `TypeError: reader.read is not a function`

maya: repro steps? which SDK version and how are you bundling the app?

owen: sdk@0.8.2 from npm. Repro repo: Expo bare workflow, EAS build disabled (local devclient). metro config: default, no extra aliases. Steps: 1) yarn add @redwoodinference/sdk 2) import { createClient } from '@redwoodinference/sdk' 3) call client.chat.stream(...) and pipe response body to a ReadableStream (native fetch). On Hermes the crypto error shows up earlier on first call that uses `randomUUID` inside the SDK. On JSC it goes further then fails on stream consumption.

alex: sounds like the usual RN/Expo polyfill gap. Two fixes we've used: (1) add `react-native-get-random-values` and call `import 'react-native-get-random-values'` at app entry, (2) for streams use `react-native-blob-util` or a fetch-polyfill that surfaces `ReadableStream`. Hermes's fetch isn't fully spec-compatible for streaming.

sam: we should probably make the SDK more defensive. Quick patch we used internally: at runtime do `if (!globalThis.crypto || !globalThis.crypto.getRandomValues) { try { require('react-native-get-random-values'); } catch (_) { /* noop, best-effort */ } }` That avoids an ESM-only import problem by using `require` if present. But note: in ESM-only consumers `require` might not exist.

jess: TS/typing gotcha too: TS errors in RN because `lib.dom`'s `Crypto` shape differs. Consumers see `Property 'subtle' does not exist on type 'Crypto'` when we refer to `crypto.subtle` in SDK types. For RN we ship the same types and tsc complains. Workarounds: add `skipLibCheck: true` for apps, or the SDK could use narrower types (declare `declare const globalThis: any` in the runtime wrapper) or publish a separate `index.cjs.d.ts` with conditional types.

maya: Can you paste minimal metro/babel tweaks that worked for you?

owen: metro.config.js I tried (worked partially):
```js
// metro.config.js
const { getDefaultConfig } = require('expo/metro-config');
const config = getDefaultConfig(__dirname);
config.resolver.extraNodeModules = {
  crypto: require.resolve('react-native-crypto'),
  stream: require.resolve('stream-browserify')
};
module.exports = config;
```
Then in App.tsx top: `import 'react-native-get-random-values'; global.Buffer = global.Buffer || require('buffer').Buffer;` That fixed the crypto error but streaming is still flaky unless I use `react-native-blob-util` and avoid `fetch` streaming.

alex: two follow-ups for SDK team (short):
- Add a tiny runtime shim (CJS/UMD-friendly) that does the safe `globalThis.crypto` check and attempts to polyfill via known RN packages. That should be loaded only when environment detection says RN/Hermes.
- Add a short docs page under DevEx: "React Native / Expo notes" listing required polyfills and recommended patterns (e.g., prefer `response.arrayBuffer()` for now rather than `ReadableStream` piping).

sam: I'm happy to PR the runtime guard. Concern: package is ESM-first; using `require` in published ESM may upset bundlers. We can ship both entrypoints: `main` (cjs) with shim side-effect and `module` (esm) for tree-shaking. Or a separate tiny package `@redwoodinference/sdk-rn-shim` that apps can `import` when on RN.

jess: for typings I'll open a draft PR that wraps the SDK's `crypto` usage behind a type guard and exports a `declare global { interface Global { crypto?: any } }` ambient declaration in our `types/rn-shim.d.ts`. That will keep downstream TS from exploding.

owen: awesome. I'll try the temporary app-level fixes and link a repro. I filed a GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/2197 (contains repro + logs).

maya: perfect. tagging @devex for docs update request and linking the issue in the doc PR. :thumbsup:

alex: tiny note: include a test in our E2E matrix that runs a minimal RN Expo example on CI (Hermes) so we catch regressions. Even a smoke `yarn build` + simple node harness that imports the SDK and checks `typeof globalThis.crypto` could catch this.

sam: agreed. I'll add a TODO in the infra board.

jess: PRs incoming: runtime guard + types shim + docs. Will link once ready.

owen: thanks everyone — saved me a ton of time. I'll drop updates in the GH issue as I test the patches.
